### Phase-12 state-1 brainstorm

Brainstorm session decisions (THIS commit), all per the user's standing preferences `feedback_pick_recommendation` ("always pick the recommended option; do not ask") and `feedback_execution_style` ("default to subagent-driven-development; skip the two-option fork" — applies to state-3, not this state-1 controller-run brainstorm). This is the **fourth post-MVP-trunk feature-family brainstorm session** (after phase-09 `3025594` + phase-10 `c73f44f` + phase-11 `1370aaa`; the latter is the freshest shape precedent). The pick was made directly per `feedback_pick_recommendation` — no two-option fork; the alternatives + 5-dimension scoring are documented below.

- **Family pick: Upstream robustness family (FIRST concrete phase; first feature-family phase to LEAVE the HTTP-filter family).** Picked directly per `feedback_pick_recommendation`. **The decisive context shift:** the HTTP-filter family was picked three times running (09/10/11) chiefly to close the 09 REVIEW M2 H2-decoration carryforward — which CLOSED at phase 11 (the H1 + H2 HCM filter-synth writer paths are now at parity). With that driver gone, the pick is free to diversify. Applying the same 5-dimension scoring framework used at phases 09 + 10 + 11:

  - **Upstream robustness family (WINNER) — active HTTP health checking** — (a) carryforward closure **MEDIUM-HIGH** — it is the **named owner of 06.3 REVIEW I2** (the deferred synthetic-backend harness infrastructure; the REVIEW named "the upstream-robustness family" as the close site verbatim). Phase 12 makes the first down-payment (the synthetic health-aware backend); full I2 closure (per-class counter wire coverage + `upstream_cx_total` `value-exact`) remains tied to connection pooling per the REVIEW disposition. (b) foundation pressure **ZERO** — reuses tokio (already permitted) + `envoy-http1::Client` (04.3) for the probe + `envoy-config::parse_duration` + `Int64Range` + `envoy-stats`. (c) arch risk **LOW-MEDIUM** — the integration seam is **PRE-BUILT and annotated for this**: `ClusterHandle::pick_endpoint() -> Option<SocketAddr>` (`cluster.rs:152`, *"preserved for phase-06+ health checking"*) + the existing no-healthy-endpoint → synth-503 path (`router.rs:18-20`, `hcm.rs:580-582`). The genuinely-new surface is the periodic-probe task (the project's first periodic-background primitive) + the `EndpointHealth` state machine + the panic threshold. (d) contract maturity **MEDIUM** — new health-check stats + the no-healthy-upstream body need §6.2 empirical pinning. (e) scope tractability **MEDIUM (upper band; SPLIT projected)** — ~1800-2200 LoC, over the §6.1 gate → likely split into 12.1 + 12.2.
  - **Load balancing family** (`least_request` / `ring_hash` / `random` etc.) — documented "strong second-place" at phases 10 + 11 on the LoC/foundations axes, but **re-scored DOWN this brainstorm on differential-testability**: randomized LBs (`random`, default-P2C `least_request`) produce per-request endpoint picks that CANNOT be matched across two independent proxies (non-differential-testable, same class as fractional fault percentage at phase 11); the deterministic LBs (`ring_hash`, `maglev`) require EXACT hash-algorithm fidelity (xxHash / Maglev permutation) — high arch risk for differential equivalence. Any LB differential test also needs a NEW distinguishable-backend + endpoint-attribution harness primitive. (a) carryforward closure ZERO; (b) zero foundation; (c) LOW-MEDIUM but the differential-observability is fragile; (d) MEDIUM; (e) HIGH LoC tractability. **Rejected** on the differential-testability fragility + zero carryforward closure — a more careful analysis than the prior brainstorms' LoC-focused "second-place" billing.
  - **Continuing HTTP-filter family** (`cors` / `jwt_authn` / `ext_authz` / `csrf` / `compression` / `buffer`) — the low-hanging StopAndSend fruit is EXHAUSTED (header_mutation 07.2, local_ratelimit 09, rbac 10, fault 11 done). The remaining filters each need either a foundations grant (jwt_authn JOSE; oauth2 HTTPS client; compression flate2/brotli), a per-route framework extension (cors/csrf), or the gRPC family (ext_authz/ext_proc/global-rate-limit). So continuing now carries HIGHER foundation pressure / arch risk than before + the decisive 09-M2 driver is gone. **Rejected** — diversifying is the better engineering move.
  - **Network filters family** — HIGH arch risk (new network-layer filter-chain primitive) + LOW contract maturity. Rejected per the 09/10/11 reasoning.
  - **HTTP/3 + QUIC** — VERY HIGH foundation pressure (`quinn`) + VERY HIGH arch risk. Rejected.
  - **gRPC / xDS / Observability / Runtime+hot-restart / WASM / Deprecated** — same dispositions as phases 09/10/11 (unmotivated / highest-risk / multi-phase sub-project / meta-bookkeeping). Rejected.

  Top-3 viable: **Upstream robustness > Load balancing > continuing HTTP filters.** Upstream robustness wins on: closing the named-owner carryforward (06.3 I2); zero foundation pressure; the pre-built integration seam (lowering arch risk); and laying the periodic-task primitive the whole family needs. The SPEC §1 + §3 record the picked family + feature scope.

- **Feature pick: active HTTP health checking (HTTP checker only; minimum-viable).** Picked directly per `feedback_pick_recommendation`. Among the family's features (active HC / outlier detection / circuit breakers / retries / connection pooling), active HTTP health checking is the §9-listed-first + the cleanest first phase: response-based differential observable (200-through vs synth-503-no-healthy, deterministic in steady state), reuses the pre-built `pick()->Option` + synth-503 seam, and builds the periodic-probe primitive the family reuses. **Scope cuts (defer per SPEC §4):** TCP/gRPC/custom checkers; multiple health checks per cluster; outlier detection; circuit breakers; retries; connection pooling; `no_traffic_interval`/jitter/`reuse_connection`; event logging; degraded/excluded host states; HC over H2 upstream. HTTP-only + binary Healthy/Unhealthy + single fixed interval + fresh-connection-per-probe is the minimum-viable cut (consistent with the rbac "header-scope only" + fault "deterministic-only" minimum-viable discipline).

Phase `06` (`envoy-stats`) is load-bearing for the health-check stats but is implicit (the schema captures the primary direct foundations; cross-deliverable reuse — `envoy-stats`, `parse_duration`, `Int64Range` — is implicit per the phase-11 "implicit 05 dep" precedent).

- **Split-gate projection at state-2 (SPEC §6.1): LIKELY SPLIT into 12.1 + 12.2.** SPEC-time estimate ~1800-2200 LoC (production ~850, tests ~900, fixture/harness/backend ~470) — materially OVER the §6.1 ~1500-LoC gate (task count ~14-16, under ~25). **Recommended seam:** 12.1 = D1 schema + D2 validator + D3 `EndpointHealth` + D5 LB-integration + D6 stats (no new fixture; regression-equivalence via the 18 existing fixtures staying green — the 05.1/07.1 foundation-slice pattern) / 12.2 = D4 active-HC task + the new `envoy-health` crate + D7 fixture 0019 + synthetic backend + settle-driver + backstop + fuzz seed + parent-12 close. ### Phase-12 state-2 split decision

This subsection records the phase-12 state-2 PLAN-write commit (`phase 12: state-2 split decision + sub-phase SPECs (12.1/12.2) [ADR-0036, ADR-0037]`) — the fifth project SPLIT state-2 (after phases 02/03/07/08), all per the user's standing preferences `feedback_pick_recommendation` (pick the recommendation; no two-option fork) + `feedback_execution_style` (the state-2 PLAN-write is the controller's authoring pass; subagent-driven execution applies at state 3). Docs-only; 5 files; ADR-0036 (split) + ADR-0037 (no-healthy-body reconciliation); no SPEC edit to the parent-12 SPEC; no PLAN/PROGRESS (those land at the 12.1 state-2 PLAN-write next session).

**§6.2 empirical-verification findings (HEAVY; 6 items; against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`).** Performed at THIS commit by the controller directly (per the parent SPEC §6.2 + the phase-10/11-ratified verify-at-PLAN-write discipline). Methodology: a Docker bridge network with (a) a synthetic health-aware backend container (returns 200 on `/`, a configurable status on `/healthz`, logs every probe) and (b) an `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` container running an active-HC cluster pointing at the backend by container name (STRICT_DNS); admin `/stats` scraped + data-plane `GET /` probed across the convergence window. *(Initial host-networking attempts via `host.docker.internal` network-failed because it resolves IPv6-only on this Docker Desktop; resolved by co-locating both containers on a shared bridge network.)*

| # | Item | Finding | Disposition |
|---|------|---------|-------------|
| 1 | **Initial endpoint health state** (the single most load-bearing) | **Unhealthy/pending-until-first-pass.** An unhealthy backend with a 3 s probe delay → data-plane `no healthy upstream` (503) from t=0, *before* the first probe resolves. Hosts with active HC configured begin not-healthy; the first passing check (`healthy_threshold` consecutive successes) marks them healthy. | **MATCHES** the parent SPEC's recommended projection. Drives D3 (`EndpointHealth` initial state = Unhealthy) + the 12.1 inert-and-unexercised-seam note. No ADR. |
| 2 | **No-healthy-upstream synth body** (the byte-precision item) | status **503**; body **`no healthy upstream`** = **19 bytes**, hex `6e 6f 20 68 65 61 6c 74 68 79 20 75 70 73 74 72 65 61 6d`, **no trailing newline**; headers `{ content-length:19, content-type:text/plain, date, server:envoy, connection:close }`; **no wire `x-envoy-*` flag header**. | **DIVERGES from envoy-rust's existing synth-503** (`hcm.rs:918 synth_status` = EMPTY body, content-length:0). → **ADR-0037**: reconcile envoy-rust to emit the 19-byte body on the no-healthy-upstream path (impl in 12.2 D6.2, only the `hcm.rs:582` arm — NOT global `synth_status`). Fixture 0019 asserts byte-exact. |
| 3 | **Panic threshold** | default **50 %**; comparison **strictly-below** (`healthy% < threshold`: `value:0` → `0%<0%`=false → no panic → 503; default 50 % → `0%<50%`=true → panic → 200 routed to all); `Percent` shape **`{ value: <double> }`**; panic = round-robin over ALL; bonus stat `cluster.<n>.lb_healthy_panic` (not wired at phase-12 scope). | **MATCHES** projection. Drives D1 (`CommonLbConfig`/`Percent`) + D5 (panic logic). Fixture uses `{ value: 0 }` (disable panic). No ADR. |
| 4 | **Health-check stat names** | `cluster.<n>.health_check.{attempt,success,failure,passive_failure,network_failure,verify_cluster,healthy,degraded}` + `membership_{healthy,total,degraded,excluded,change}`. `membership_healthy` = count of currently-healthy endpoints (1 healthy / 0 ejected). | **MATCHES** projection. 12.1 wires the minimum-viable subset: `attempt`/`success`/`failure` counters + `membership_healthy` gauge (rest defer per parent §4). No ADR. |
| 5 | **HTTP probe shape** | `GET /healthz`, `:authority`/`Host: <cluster-name>` (default when `http_health_check.host` unset), `user-agent: Envoy/HC`; default `expected_statuses` = **exactly 200** (201 → unhealthy); `Int64Range` **half-open `[start, end)`** (`[200,201)` excludes 201; `[200,202)` includes it — reusable directly). | **MATCHES** projection. Drives D1 (`HttpHealthCheck`) + D4 (probe). No ADR. |
| 6 | **Duration config shape** | Envoy accepts decimal-second protobuf-JSON durations (`1s`/`0.5s`/`0.25s`) but **REJECTS `500ms`**; envoy-rust's `parse_duration` accepts `1s`/`500ms`/`500us` (integer + s/ms/us) but **REJECTS `0.5s`** (parses the numeric part as `u64`). **Shared form = integer seconds only.** | **DIVERGES from the parent SPEC fixture sketch's `interval: 0.5s`** (which envoy-rust would reject). → **PLAN-time correction (no ADR):** the 12.2 fixture uses integer-second durations (`interval: 1s`, `timeout: 1s`) on both sides (identical YAMLs); 12.1 reuses `parse_duration` as-is (no `0.5s` support added — scope creep). |

**Disposition:** items 1/3/4/5 MATCHED → no ADR. Item 2 → **ADR-0037** (the load-bearing wire-level body bytes pinned; the ADR-0034-class durability decision; reconcile-by-implementation per D-3.3). Item 6 → PLAN-time fixture-shape correction (no ADR). DECISIONS.md ledger head **ADR-0035 → ADR-0037** (ADR-0036 split + ADR-0037 reconciliation, consecutive numbers at this commit per the parent SPEC §6.2 "if both fire at the PLAN-write commit").

**Split-gate verdict.** Parent SPEC §6.1 ~1800-2200 LoC, materially over the §6.1 ~1500 gate → **SPLIT into 12.1 + 12.2** (the recommended seam), per `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §6.2. Mirrors the parent-07 `6db5a01` + parent-08 `56dee82` 2-way-split shape (the fifth project 2-way split). Parent ROADMAP row 12 → `in-progress` + `sub-phases: 12.1, 12.2`; two sub-phase rows added (`planned`); STATE → `12.1` state 2 (skipping a 12.1 state-1 brainstorm, per the parent-07/08 precedent — the parent SPEC already brainstormed the full surface).

**The split seam:**
- **12.1 (`12.1-endpoint-health-and-lb-integration`)** = D1 schema (`HealthCheck`/`HttpHealthCheck`/`CommonLbConfig`/`Percent`; reuses `parse_duration` + `Int64Range`) + D2 validator (~4-6 `ConfigError` variants) + D3 `EndpointHealth` (envoy-cluster; initial Unhealthy) + D5 LB-integration (`pick()` excludes unhealthy + panic threshold) + D6 stats (`membership_healthy` gauge; the 3 counters land at 12.1 or 12.2 per the PLAN-writer's D6 lock-in) + the `parse_bootstrap` corpus seed (18→19). **No new fixture** — regression-equivalence via the 18 existing fixtures (the 05.1/07.1 foundation-slice pattern; machinery inert when unconfigured). ~900-1000 LoC. **Subtle consequence of the item-1 finding:** in the 12.1-only world a *configured*-HC cluster has no probe task to mark its endpoints healthy, so 12.1 ships NO configured-HC fixture/test (the path stays inert-and-unexercised until 12.2 wires the probe task + fixture together — the 07.1 unused-`StopAndSend` discipline).
- **12.2 (`12.2-active-http-probe-and-fixture`)** = D4 active-HC probe task + the new `envoy-health` crate (clean DAG over envoy-cluster + envoy-http1 + envoy-config + envoy-stats + tokio; no cycle; the project's first periodic-background primitive; reuses `envoy-http1::Client`) + D6.2 the no-healthy-upstream body reconciliation (ADR-0037 impl) + D7.1 fixture 0019 + the synthetic health-aware backend harness primitive (the 06.3 REVIEW I2 down-payment) + the settle-then-probe driver + Docker wrapper + D7.3 in-process backstop (both convergence directions) + parent-12 close. ~1000-1200 LoC.

### Phase-13 state-1 brainstorm

**Family pick.** `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §9 enumerates the eight feature families. At the post-12.2 close-out boundary the slate is fully open — all MVP-trunk phases 00-08 + the three HTTP-filter-family phases (09 `local_ratelimit`, 10 `rbac`, 11 `fault`) + the first Upstream-robustness-family phase (parent-12; sub-phases 12.1 + 12.2) all stand `done`. The candidates for the next phase were: (i) continue the Upstream-robustness family with `13-outlier-detection` (per-endpoint ejection on consecutive 5xx / per-host success-rate thresholds — natural family-list order after active HC) OR `13-connection-pooling` (per-protocol upstream connection pools — the named-owner phase for 06.3 REVIEW I2's residual); (ii) enter a new family (HTTP/3+QUIC, gRPC, xDS, Observability, Runtime+hot-restart, WASM-host).

**Five-dimension scoring:**

| Dimension | `13-outlier-detection` | `13-connection-pooling` | new family (HTTP/3+QUIC, gRPC, xDS, Observability, Runtime, WASM) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Carryforward closure value** | Zero (no named carryforward closes). Outlier detection is a fresh subsystem; would reuse the 12.1 `EndpointHealth` ejection seam but doesn't close anything from the standing inventory. | **HIGH.** Connection pooling is the **named-owner phase for 06.3 REVIEW I2 residual** per the 06.3 REVIEW.md §3 disposition + the 12.2 down-payment scoping. Closes BOTH (a) per-class `downstream_rq_3xx/4xx/5xx` + `cluster.<name>.upstream_rq_5xx` wire bilateral coverage AND (b) `cluster.<name>.upstream_cx_total` `value-exact` tightening. This is the single highest-value closure currently available in the standing inventory. | Zero direct closures. Some families surface their own internal carryforwards (e.g. Observability would tighten the StatsTagExtractor allow-list residual) but none close the 06.3 I2 residual. |
| **Foundation pressure (new top-level Cargo deps)** | LOW. Reuses the 12.1 `EndpointHealth` ejection seam + the 12.2 periodic-task primitive. No new crate. No ADR. | **LOW.** Reuses the 12.2 `HealthAwareHttp1Backend` harness primitive (extend in place) + the existing `ConnGaugeGuard` RAII pattern + `envoy-http1::Client` + `envoy-http2::Client`. Pool primitives live inside `envoy-http1`/`envoy-http2` (`pool.rs` modules). No new top-level Cargo dep. No new ADR projected at SPEC time (conditional ADR-0038 split LIKELY at PLAN-write; conditional ADR-0039 §6.2 revision PLAUSIBLE). | HIGH (variable). HTTP/3+QUIC needs `quinn` foundations grant; gRPC needs additional `tonic` features; xDS needs from-scratch state-machine atop `tonic` transport; Observability needs OTLP/Datadog/XRay; Runtime+hot-restart is significant new infrastructure; WASM-host is its own multi-phase sub-project. Each new family carries a foundations-grant ADR. |
| **Architectural risk** | MEDIUM. The passive-vs-active distinction is subtle (outlier detection observes data-plane responses; doesn't probe); needs careful interaction with the 12-active path. Cross-proxy timing-dependent ejection windows are hard to make deterministic for the differential harness (would need §Timing tolerances opt-in). | **MEDIUM-HIGH.** Pool primitives are the most-complex piece — H2 multiplexed-streams pool with peer-SETTINGS coordination + GOAWAY handling. But the surface is well-understood (Envoy's pool model is documented) + the per-protocol crate placement avoids cycles cleanly. The `upstream_cx_total` increment-site migration (from per-call to per-connection at pool create) is mechanical but must be atomic to avoid double-counting. The cycle-resolution decision (§5.1) is well-anticipated. | HIGH (variable). HTTP/3 introduces a new downstream listener type + a new conformance suite. gRPC complicates the H2 path. xDS introduces dynamic-config state. WASM is a full ABI + engine binding effort. |
| **Contract-surface maturity** | The `outlier_detection.*` Envoy stat tree is documented but timing-dependent. Differential observability is largely stats-based (which counter increments on which trigger) + ejection-window-bounded — harder than connection-pooling's deterministic-pool-state observable. | **HIGH.** The `cluster.<name>.upstream_cx_*` stat tree is fully documented + matures cleanly under pooling. Per-class HCM counters are already 06.3-defined and BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT-locked; phase 13 just realizes them at fixture level. The synthetic-backend pattern is 12.2-precedented. | Variable. xDS has the most mature contract (ADS state machine + effective-config diff). Observability and Runtime have moderate maturity. WASM is least-mature (ABI conformance suite still evolving upstream). |
| **First-phase scope tractability** | Tractable as a single phase if scoped to consecutive-5xx ejection only (split-gate plausible at PLAN-write but not certain). Reuses 12.x infrastructure heavily. | **MEDIUM.** ~1800-2400 LoC projected — over the §6.1 ~1500 gate. SPLIT into 13.1 + 13.2 LIKELY at PLAN-write (recommended seam: H1-only / H2-only, alternative seam: foundation-slice). Each sub-phase comes in at ~1000-1200 LoC each — manageable. | Variable. xDS family is its own multi-phase sub-project at minimum. Observability could fit as ~3 sub-phases. Runtime+hot-restart is moderate. WASM is multi-phase by design. HTTP/3+QUIC is moderate (probably 2 sub-phases — downstream H3 + upstream H3). |

**Decision: `13-connection-pooling`.** Per `feedback_pick_recommendation` (always pick the recommendation; no two-option fork). The recommendation is unambiguously connection pooling because: (1) it's the **named-owner phase for the highest-value standing carryforward** (06.3 REVIEW I2 residual, deferred from 06.3 and named again at 12.2); (2) it **reuses the freshest landed harness primitive** (12.2's `HealthAwareHttp1Backend`); (3) its scope is **tractable with a known SPLIT seam** (H1-only / H2-only at sub-phase 13.1/13.2); (4) the **foundation pressure is LOW** (no new top-level Cargo dep; pool primitives are protocol-internal); (5) it **continues the Upstream-robustness family** in a natural way (active HC at 12 → pooling at 13; outlier detection + circuit breakers + retries defer to follow-up phases — all reuse the 12.x + 13.x infrastructure when they land). The decision is **NOT** "outlier detection" — outlier detection has zero carryforward closure value and timing-dependent observability that the differential harness handles less cleanly; it defers to a follow-up Upstream-robustness phase. The decision is **NOT** "enter a new family" — the project's standing posture (per `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §9 family ordering + the established Carryforward-closure-value-first heuristic from the 11/12 brainstorms) favors closing named residuals before opening new families when both are tractable.

**§6.2 empirical-verification findings (HEAVY; 9 items; against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`).** Performed at THIS commit by the controller directly (per the parent SPEC §6.2 + the phase-10/11/12-ratified verify-at-PLAN-write discipline). Methodology: a Docker bridge network (`p13net`) with (a) a Python-based configurable HTTP/1.1 backend container (Python 3.12-alpine; `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` with `protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"` for keep-alive support; serves 200 on `/`, 301/404/500/503 on `/301`/`/404`/`/500`/`/503`, configurable status on `/healthz` via `HEALTHZ_STATUS` env) and (b) an `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` container running an HTTP/1.1 HCM listener routing through a STRICT_DNS cluster with `circuit_breakers: { thresholds: [{ priority: DEFAULT, max_connections: 2 }] }` pointing at the backend container by container name; admin `/stats` + `/config_dump` scraped + data-plane requests driven from the host via curl + Python `http.client.HTTPConnection`. *(Initial container-name resolution attempts via `backend` failed because Docker's DNS resolves the container's full name `p13-backend`; resolved by updating the YAML.)* For item (vi) — H2 cluster stats namespace — booted a second Envoy with `typed_extension_protocol_options.envoy.extensions.upstreams.http.v3.HttpProtocolOptions.explicit_http_config.http2_protocol_options: {}` and scraped the cluster stat namespace (no H2C backend reach needed; the stat names are registered at cluster-construct time).

| # | Item | Finding | Disposition |
|---|------|---------|-------------|
| i | **`circuit_breakers.thresholds` shape + max_connections default** | `circuit_breakers: { thresholds: [{ priority?: <RoutingPriority>, max_connections?: u32, max_pending_requests?: u32, max_requests?: u32, max_retries?: u32, ... }] }`. The `priority` field defaults to `DEFAULT` (and is omitted from `/config_dump` when DEFAULT). `max_connections` default 1024 (per Envoy docs; not observed empirically because the harness load is below the cap). | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. Schema D1 lands as projected (`Cluster.circuit_breakers: Option<CircuitBreakers>` with `Thresholds` carrying `priority?: Option<RoutingPriority>` + `max_connections?: Option<u32>`; phase-13 supports DEFAULT + max_connections only; other threshold fields rejected by `deny_unknown_fields`). No ADR. |
| ii | **H1 default pool behavior under NO `circuit_breakers`** | Envoy ALWAYS pools regardless of `circuit_breakers` config (a no-`circuit_breakers` cluster + 5 requests over a single downstream keep-alive conn → `upstream_cx_total: 1`; full pool reuse). `circuit_breakers` is OPTIONAL at config-time; absence means defaults. `/config_dump` shows `circuit_breakers: "<absent>"` when not configured (Envoy doesn't echo defaults). | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. § 5.4 default-enabled-pool decision: phase-13's H1 pool runs **with hardcoded defaults when `circuit_breakers` is absent** (NOT pool-gated by the field). The 19 existing fixtures (none configures `circuit_breakers`) pool transparently. Regression-equivalence guaranteed by the existing presence-only `upstream_cx_total` assertions (no value-exact assertion to regress). No ADR. |
| iii | **H1 idle_timeout knob + default** | Knob lives at `typed_extension_protocol_options.envoy.extensions.upstreams.http.v3.HttpProtocolOptions.common_http_protocol_options.idle_timeout` (a Duration; nested deep). NOT at the cluster top-level. Default: 1 hour (3600s) per upstream Envoy docs. /config_dump shows `<absent>` for the nested field when not explicitly set. | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. §4 deferral: phase-13 (13.1 + 13.2) does NOT add the config-side `idle_timeout` knob; the pool uses a hardcoded sensible default (60s — short enough to test idle eviction in a deterministic test, long enough to not fire under fixture settle windows). The config-side knob defers to a follow-up phase. No ADR. |
| iv | **`upstream_cx_total` increment semantics + discriminating differential observable** | One increment per established upstream TCP connection. Discriminating observable shape: with a **SINGLE downstream keep-alive conn** issuing 5 sequential requests → `upstream_cx_total: 1` (full pool reuse via 1 upstream connection). With **separate downstream conns** (curl invocations) → `upstream_cx_total: N` (one upstream connect per downstream-side conn — Envoy's H1 pool returns the connection to idle AFTER the downstream conn closes, by which point the next downstream conn has already triggered a fresh upstream connect). Concurrent 4 curl jobs with `max_connections: 2` → `upstream_cx_total: 4` + `upstream_cx_overflow: 2` (max_connections is ADVISORY: Envoy increments the overflow counter but still completes the request). | **MATCHES** SPEC projection but with **CRITICAL NUANCE**. **PLAN-time fixture-shape lock-in:** fixture 0020 driver MUST issue multiple requests over a SINGLE downstream keep-alive conn to make `upstream_cx_total` the discriminating differential observable (1 vs. N). The differential harness's existing `Driver::Http1` opens one conn per request — **13.1 D10 extends the driver with `Driver::Http1KeepAlive`** (~30 LoC; mirrors 12.2's `Driver::Http1AfterSettle` precedent). NOT a wire-contract change → NO ADR fires. |
| v | **`upstream_cx_destroy` + sibling counter names + fire-sites** | Full sibling set per-cluster: `upstream_cx_destroy`, `_destroy_local`, `_destroy_remote`, `_destroy_with_active_rq`, `_destroy_local_with_active_rq`, `_destroy_remote_with_active_rq`, `upstream_cx_close_notify` (counts peer-initiated Connection: close). All fire when a pool connection is destroyed (different sub-counters for local-initiated vs remote-initiated destruction; the per-`_with_active_rq` variants fire only when destruction happens while a request was outstanding). All per-cluster (NOT per-endpoint). | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. D7 (stats): phase-13 wires the parent `upstream_cx_destroy` (always-fire sibling) + `upstream_cx_http1_total` (H1 pool connect counter) + the 13.2-landed `upstream_cx_http2_total`. The 5 sub-siblings defer to follow-up phases (no fixture deterministically forces local-vs-remote-destroy at phase-13 scope). No ADR. |
| vi | **H2 pool default behavior + max_concurrent_streams + multi-conn per endpoint** | H2 cluster stat namespace (no H2 traffic needed; Envoy registers at cluster-construct time): `cluster.<n>.upstream_cx_http1_total` (always registered; even on H2 cluster — for cross-protocol fallback), `upstream_cx_http2_total` (H2 partition), `upstream_cx_http3_total` (H3 — registered for future use). Default `max_concurrent_streams`: Envoy-as-client honors peer's `SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS` (default 100 per RFC 7540 §6.5.2 if peer doesn't send SETTINGS). Per-endpoint multi-conn threshold: Envoy spawns 2nd upstream H2 conn only when 1st is at peer's cap. Legacy cluster-field `http2_protocol_options` stays absent in `/config_dump` when `typed_extension_protocol_options` is used (Envoy's modern path). | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. 13.2 D5 H2 pool primitive design: per-endpoint connection list with `active_streams: AtomicU32` tracking + spawn 2nd conn only when 1st at peer's `SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS` cap (or cluster's `max_connections` cap, whichever is lower). 13.2 D7.2 lands the `cluster.<n>.upstream_cx_http2_total` BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT row. No ADR. |

Listener-namespace mirror: `listener.0.0.0.0_10000.http.ingress_http.downstream_rq_{2,3,4,5}xx` — same values. **Cycle-resolution decision (PLAN lock-in #1) — picked per `feedback_pick_recommendation`:** the 13.1 SPEC §5.1 left the seam open between (a) a new trait declared in `envoy-cluster` (`H1ClientPool` trait implemented by `envoy-http1::H1Pool`; held as `Cluster.h1_pool: Option<Arc<dyn H1ClientPool>>`) vs (b) bin-wired injection via an external `H1PoolManager` registry sibling-to-`ClusterManager`. PLAN-time PICK: option (b). Rationale: (1) option (a) requires interior mutability on `Cluster` (the `Arc<Cluster>` from `from_bootstrap` has no setter), OR widening `from_bootstrap`'s signature to take a `pool_builder` callback, OR chicken-and-egg pre-building with `Cluster.cx_total` registration — all intrusive. (2) option (b) parallels the 12.2 `envoy-health::Scheduler` precedent verbatim — `envoy-bin` builds `cluster_mgr` first via `from_bootstrap`, then `H1PoolManager::for_bootstrap` second (walks bootstrap clusters; looks up each in `cluster_mgr` to grab shared `Arc<Counter>`/`Arc<Gauge>` stat handles; builds one `H1Pool` per H1 cluster); the HCM proxy arm gets the pool manager plumbed alongside `cluster_mgr` at HCM-config construction. (3) NO new trait in `envoy-cluster`; only `ConnGaugeGuard` gains a public `from_gauge` constructor (4-line addition) so pools can construct guards against the shared cluster gauge handle. (4) NO new top-level Cargo dep (per lock-in #9). (5) NO ADR fires (per lock-in #16). If state-3 execution surfaces a non-obvious lifecycle complication (e.g. the HCM-config-construction site has poor ergonomic reach to `Arc<H1PoolManager>`), the controller documents the surfacing finding in PROGRESS + lands an inline ADR resolving it (NOT projected).

Pre-fix, `H2PoolGuard::Drop` ran `active_streams.fetch_sub(1)` OUTSIDE the `connections.lock()`, opening a window where a concurrent Phase-1 walker in `acquire()` could CAS-claim the stream slot on the to-be-evicted entry, leading to orphaned PoolGuards with broken `established` accounting and falsely-fired `cx_destroy`. Post-fix the invalidate branch takes `connections.lock()` BEFORE the fetch_sub and holds it across both the decrement and the `retain()`. The non-invalidate branch keeps the original lock-free fetch_sub (residual race benign by the sweeper's `active_streams != 0` early-return invariant; documented in a correctness-argument comment block). Also added an H1 race-regression stress test `pool_acquire_after_concurrent_release_1000_iterations_zero_spurious_overflows` (probabilistic 1000-iter exercise of the pre-fix race window; post-fix produces 0 spurious overflows; runs in ~90ms). 3 files touched (+144 / -16 LoC net).

### Phase-14 state-1 brainstorm

**Family pick.** At the post-parent-13-close boundary (`96630f9`) the slate was fully open — all MVP-trunk phases 00-08 + the three HTTP-filter-family phases (09 `local_ratelimit`, 10 `rbac`, 11 `fault`) + the first two Upstream-robustness-family phases (parent-12; sub-phases 12.1 + 12.2 + parent-13; sub-phases 13.1 + 13.2) all stand `done`. The standing posture options enumerated in the previous-session "Next expected skill" block (STATE.md before THIS commit) were: **(A)** continued Upstream-robustness — outlier detection / circuit breakers expansion / retries+hedging / TCP-proxy connection pooling; **(B)** HTTP/3 + QUIC new family; **(C)** gRPC new family; **(D)** xDS / dynamic config new family; **(E)** Observability new family; **(F)** Runtime + hot restart new family; **(G)** WASM host new family; **(H)** ADR-0028 closure as a foundations-pivot phase. Per `feedback_pick_recommendation` (always pick the recommendation; no two-option fork), the controller picked **(A) continued Upstream-robustness — outlier detection variants**, the seeded family member named first in ROADMAP §9 ("Upstream robustness family — active health checks, **outlier detection variants**, circuit breakers, retries + hedging, per-protocol connection pooling"). The within-(A) sub-pick (outlier detection vs circuit breakers expansion vs retries vs TCP-proxy pooling) settled on **outlier detection** because: (1) it is the natural next variant in the parent-charter list (active HC at 12 → connection pooling at 13 → outlier detection is the next-named primitive); (2) it **maximally reuses the 12.x + 13.x infrastructure**: the 12.1 `EndpointHealth` ejection seam at `pick()` + the 12.2 no-healthy-upstream synth-503 path + the 13.x configurable-status synthetic backend + the 13.1 `Driver::Http1KeepAlive` harness driver are all reused verbatim — no new harness primitive is required; (3) it **introduces the project's fourth periodic-background primitive** (the ejection sweeper) extending the 12.2 + 13.1 + 13.2 triad cleanly (identical `tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken` cancellation discipline); (4) the scope is **tractable** at ~1500-2100 LoC with a known SPLIT seam (foundation slice 14.1 = schema + state machine + LB integration + stats; observable-behavior slice 14.2 = response-receipt hooks + ejection sweeper + fixture + parent-14 close — the standing 12/13 cadence); (5) the **foundation pressure is LOW** (no new top-level Cargo dep; the new `outlier.rs` module is internal to `envoy-cluster`); (6) **no foundations grant required** (D-3.2 hand-rolled scratch mandate — outlier detection is on the from-scratch list); (7) it **defers the more architecturally fraught variants** (success-rate-based + failure-percentage-based ejection — sliding-window aggregates; `consecutive_local_origin_failure` — connect-level error-class accounting; `enforcing_*` knobs — runtime-fractional-percent enforcement) cleanly via `deny_unknown_fields`. The within-family alternatives (circuit breakers expansion — smaller scope but less family momentum; retries + hedging — larger scope, mid-request mutation; TCP-proxy connection pooling — closes the 13.2 D7.1 row's TCP carve-out but is a TCP-side feature not an upstream-robustness feature) all defer to follow-up phases.

**ADR-0028 closure NOT picked at THIS session.** Option (H) — extracting `envoy-http2::Client` into a new `envoy-http-client` crate to break the dep cycle blocking H1-listener × H2-cluster dispatch — is the documented closure path from ADR-0039 Consequences. It remains a future foundations-pivot phase (named owner: a follow-up phase, NOT phase 14). Phase-14 stays a feature phase.

**Critical scoping finding → ADR-0042 (landed at THIS commit).** The brainstorm verified the code directly (read-only `Explore` survey + controller verification of `crates/envoy-http1/src/pool.rs:177-398` + `crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:525-559`) and found the charter framing *"`max_connections` — parsed but NOT enforced"* **FALSE at HEAD `b575bdc35`**: the cap is ALREADY ENFORCED, landed at phase 13 — `H1Pool::acquire`/`H2Pool::acquire` check `established >= max_connections` → `PoolError::Overflow`; `for_bootstrap` sources the cap from `circuit_breakers.thresholds[0].max_connections` (default 1024); both router arms reject overflow with a synth-503; the schema + validator landed at 13.1. **Phase 15 therefore re-scopes from *implement-enforcement* to *observability + differential-coverage*:** (1) two minimum-viable circuit-breaker stats — `cluster.<name>.upstream_cx_overflow` (counter, at the pool cap-check site) + `cluster.<name>.circuit_breakers.default.cx_open` (gauge, edge-driven; the 14.1 namespace-subset precedent — emit the names Envoy emits for the breaker enforced, allow-list the rest); (2) the project's first CONCURRENT differential driver `Driver::Http1Concurrent` (+ a `--hold-ms` backend knob) to force concurrent upstream-connection demand > cap, since every existing driver is sequential and cannot trip it; (3) a schema carve-out accepting `max_pending_requests: 0` ONLY (the no-queue config making Envoy reject overflow immediately, matching envoy-rust, WITHOUT the deferred pending-request queue); (4) fixture `0023-upstream-circuit-breaker-max-connections` (K=2 concurrent / cap=1, single-endpoint cluster) proving the `{200, 503}` status multiset + `upstream_cx_overflow: 1` bilaterally. ADR-0042 records the finding + the minimum-viable scope boundary (defers: `max_pending_requests>0` queue; `max_requests`; `max_retries`/`retry_budget`; `max_connection_pools`; `track_remaining`/`remaining_*`; non-DEFAULT priority; per-endpoint-vs-per-cluster `cx_open` reconciliation). The brainstorm-time ADR is a cadence DEPARTURE from phases 12/13/14 (whose brainstorms landed no ADR), justified by the non-obvious scope finding per D-3.5 + the cold-readability correction of the durable record per D-3.4.

**§6.1 split-gate: projected NO SPLIT** (~12–16 tasks; ~950–1300 LoC; under the ~25-task / ~1500-LoC gate). The split valve is held in reserve (SPEC §6.1 seam: `15.1` schema + observability foundation / `15.2` concurrent driver + fixture + parent close → ADR-0044 if it fires). **depends-on `04 05 06 13`.** ROADMAP gains row `15` `planned` ONLY (no existing-row flip; row `15` enters `in-progress` at the NEXT session's state-2 PLAN-write per invariant 4.1.3).

### Phase-15 state-2 PLAN-write

THIS commit is the **phase-15 state-2 standalone PLAN-write** (`phase 15: state-2 standalone PLAN-write — PLAN.md + PROGRESS.md skeleton + Task 1 preamble [ADR-0043]`) per `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §5 state 2 + `SKILL_ROUTING.md` state 2 + `superpowers:writing-plans` + `feedback_pick_recommendation` (no fork) + `feedback_execution_style` (the state-3 implementation is subagent-driven; this controller-direct PLAN-write dispatched ONE foreground general-purpose subagent for the §6.2 Docker verification per the 14.x precedent). Controller-direct (no implementer subagents at state 2).

**The HEAVY §6.2 empirical verification falsified the SPEC's central premise → ADR-0043 (landed at THIS commit).** A foreground general-purpose subagent ran `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (sibling-container Docker topology — `host.docker.internal` resolved to an unreachable IPv6 on this macOS host) against a `max_connections:1` + `max_pending_requests:0` cluster + concurrent/sequential drivers + admin `/stats` scrapes + a `%RESPONSE_FLAGS%` access log + `curl -i`/`wc -c`/`hexdump` body capture + a control run with `max_pending_requests` removed. **Findings 1/2/3 diverged materially:**

1. **`max_pending_requests:0` rejects EVERY request** (K=1, K=2, sequential) with a 503 — NOT "serve one, reject the over-cap one." The pool never warms; the backend is never contacted; `upstream_cx_total:0`, `upstream_cx_overflow:0`. The live counter is **`cluster.<name>.upstream_rq_pending_overflow`** (= reject count). (Control — `max_pending_requests` removed, default 1024, cap=1, K=2 → both served 200, `upstream_cx_overflow:1`, `upstream_cx_total:2`: the cap-overflow connection demand is COUNTED in `upstream_cx_overflow` but then QUEUED as pending and SERVED.)
2. The overflow-503 body is **NON-EMPTY**: the byte-exact 81-byte `upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. reset reason: overflow` (no trailing newline) + the `x-envoy-overloaded: true` header. The `UO` (UpstreamOverflow) flag is access-log-only; on the wire it surfaces as `x-envoy-overloaded`.
3. There is **no `max_connections` config** under which both proxies produce an identical response-status multiset on the overflow path WITHOUT the deferred pending-request queue (Envoy queues a cap-overflow → may serve 200; envoy-rust 503s immediately). The SPEC's bilateral `{200,503}` fixture is unachievable as specified.

**Findings 4–7 matched the projection** (no SPEC revision): `cx_open` at-cap inclusive (`1` when `upstream_cx_active == max_connections`); `max_connections` per-cluster/per-priority (single-endpoint fixture coincides); full `circuit_breakers.*` = 10 always-emitted gauges (`{default,high}.{cx_open, cx_pool_open, rq_open, rq_pending_open, rq_retry_open}`); overflow-rejected request does NOT increment `upstream_cx_total`.

### Phase-16 state-1 brainstorm

THIS subsection landed at the **phase-16 state-1 NEW-PHASE brainstorm** (commit `phase 16: state-1 brainstorm — http-retries SPEC.md (Upstream-robustness family; HTTP retry policy retry_on/num_retries + upstream_rq_retry* stats + x-envoy-attempt-count + fixture 0024) [ADR-0044]`), which advanced the Active-phase pointer from "AWAITING NEXT PLANNING" to phase `16` state-1-complete / state-2-next. It records the family-pick + feature-pick rationale, the critical body-replay feasibility finding (ratified in ADR-0044), the §6.1 split projection, and the carryforward inputs consulted.

**The pick — phase `16 — HTTP retries` (the FIFTH concrete Upstream-robustness-family phase).** With phases 12 (active HTTP health checking) / 13 (per-protocol connection pooling H1+H2) / 14 (outlier detection consecutive-5xx/gateway-failure) / 15 (circuit-breaker observability + `max_pending_requests:0` reject) all `done`, the brainstorm continued the Upstream-robustness family with **HTTP retries** — the `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §9 charter's *"retries + hedging"* member. **Alternatives weighed + rejected for the next pick:** (a) open a NEW family (HTTP/3+QUIC, gRPC, xDS, Observability, Runtime+hot-restart, WASM-host) — rejected as the next pick (large foundation lifts; high architectural risk; better taken deliberately AFTER the in-flight family is wrapped; remain seeded §9 headings); (b) circuit-breaker-budget expansion (`max_requests`/`max_retries`/`track_remaining`/multi-priority + the pending-request queue) or TCP-proxy pooling — rejected for the next pick because `max_retries` (the retry circuit breaker) DEPENDS on retries existing (so retries comes first), the pending-queue is the more complex deferred surface, and TCP-proxy pooling is a narrower opportunistic close; (c) the FULL Envoy retry surface — rejected as over-scoped (bundles `per_try_timeout`, custom back-off, retry budgets, host-predicates, header overrides, hedging — blows the §6.1 gate). **Chosen rationale:** retries is the family's natural capstone at the LOWEST architectural risk (a retry loop wraps the EXISTING H1 `hcm.rs:465-706` + H2 `hcm.rs:238-481` dispatch seams — no new crate/transport/periodic-background primitive), the HIGHEST foundation reuse (the 12.x health + 14.x ejection `pick_endpoint()` seam, the 13.x pools, the 14.2 `record_response` hook, the 04.2 config patterns, the configurable-status synthetic backend), an excellent TIMING-ROBUST differential (a single GET against a 503→200 stateful backend — no concurrency, avoiding the phase-15 concurrent-driver flakiness vector), and it UNBLOCKS the deferred `max_retries` circuit-breaker budget.

**Critical scoping finding — the body-replay feasibility finding (ADR-0044).** A retry feature is feasible only if a failed request is replayable. A read-only `Explore` subagent survey + controller cross-check found retries are ALREADY body-replay-safe: **H1 DRAINS the downstream body and dispatches an EMPTY body** (`crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:401-420`, `:488`; chunked rejected with synth-501 at `:375-381` — a phase-04.3 scope choice), and **H2 BUFFERS the body and dispatches a CLONE** (`crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:153-162`, `:290`). **Phase 16 therefore needs NO new request-body buffering machinery** — the retry loop re-sends the same captured request shape per attempt. This non-obvious finding (analogous to phase-15's "enforcement-already-landed-at-13") makes a minimum-viable retry phase tractable as a single un-split (or thin 2-way-split) phase. The minimum-viable scope (ADR-0044): deliver retry-on-(`5xx`/`gateway-error`/`connect-failure`/`reset`/`retriable-status-codes`) + `num_retries` + `retriable_status_codes` + the 3-stat subset (`upstream_rq_retry{,_success,_limit_exceeded}`) + the per-attempt `upstream_rq_total`/`upstream_rq_5xx` counting reconciliation (§6.2-CRITICAL) + `x-envoy-attempt-count` + a default back-off + fixture 0024 (success + limit-exceeded). DEFER: `per_try_timeout`, custom `retry_back_off` intervals, retry budgets (`retry_budget` + `upstream_rq_retry_overflow`), `retry_priority`/`retry_host_predicate`, `x-envoy-retry-on`/`x-envoy-max-retries` overrides, vhost-level policy, `retriable_headers`, gRPC retry, and hedging.

**§6.1 split projection — single phase, but genuinely close.** SPEC-time estimate ~12–16 tasks / ~1300–1600 LoC (production ~470, tests ~600, fixture/harness/backstop ~510, docs ~120) — NEAR the §6.1 ~1500-LoC / ~25-task gate. **Projected single un-split phase, with the split valve held in reserve:** the state-2 PLAN-write re-evaluates against the §6.2-refined estimate and splits into `16.1` (config + validator + H1 retry loop + stats foundation + back-off + fixture-0024 success path) / `16.2` (H2 retry loop + per-attempt counter reconciliation + limit-exceeded coverage + parent close) + **ADR-0046** if it lands over ~1500. The §6.2 reconciliation ADR is reserved as **ADR-0045** (PLAUSIBLE — finding 4, the per-attempt `upstream_rq_total`/`5xx` counting, is the most likely trigger).

**ADR posture.** **ADR-0044 landed at THIS brainstorm commit** (the scoping ADR — the body-replay finding + the minimum-viable scope boundary; a brainstorm-time-ADR cadence mirroring phase-15's ADR-0042, justified by the non-obvious feasibility finding). DECISIONS.md ledger head advances **ADR-0043 → ADR-0044** (count 45; next available **ADR-0045**). **ADR-0028** (H1-listener × H2-cluster dispatch deferral) REMAINS OPEN — phase 16 does not engage it.

**§6.2 empirical verification (Docker `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`; foreground general-purpose subagent — the ADR-0037/0041/0043 methodology).** A retry route (`retry_on: "5xx", num_retries: 1`) + a fail-once-then-succeed backend + an always-503 backend + a NO-retry control cluster + a `%RESPONSE_FLAGS%` access log + admin `/stats`, every claim cross-checked against the real backend's per-attempt request count. ### Phase-17 state-1 brainstorm

THIS subsection landed at the **phase-17 state-1 NEW-PHASE brainstorm** (commit `phase 17: state-1 brainstorm — circuit-breaker-budgets SPEC.md (Upstream-robustness family; max_retries/max_requests/track_remaining budgets + upstream_rq_retry_overflow + breaker-state/remaining gauges + fixture 0025) [ADR-0046]`), which advanced the Active-phase pointer from "AWAITING NEXT PLANNING" to phase `17` state-1-complete / state-2-next. It records the family-pick + feature-pick rationale, the critical zero-cap-always-trips finding (ratified in ADR-0046), the §6.1 split projection, and the carryforward inputs consulted.

**The pick — phase `17 — circuit-breaker budgets` (the SIXTH concrete Upstream-robustness-family phase).** With phases 12 (active HTTP health checking) / 13 (per-protocol connection pooling H1+H2) / 14 (outlier detection) / 15 (circuit-breaker observability + `max_pending_requests:0` reject) / 16 (HTTP retries) all `done`, the brainstorm continued the Upstream-robustness family with **circuit-breaker budgets** — the promised owner phase of deferred surface enumerated in BOTH prior phases' rollovers (phase-15: *"`max_requests`/`max_retries`/`track_remaining`/multi-priority — the same budget phase"*; phase-16: *"the `max_retries` circuit breaker … the circuit-breaker-budget expansion phase, which phase 16's retries now UNBLOCK"*). **Alternatives weighed + rejected for the next pick:** (a) `per_try_timeout` (the phase-16 "prime follow-up" deferral) — too thin for a standalone phase (~400–600 LoC) AND its observable is inherently TIMING (a slow-backend-triggered per-attempt deadline), conflicting with the BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT "Timing tolerances: not compared by default" posture; better folded into a future retry-hardening phase with a non-timing primary observable; (b) pool hardening (the phase-16 carryforward family: the H1-pool `Connection: close` re-pooling gap + the H2-pool send-failure no-invalidate asymmetry + a stateful H2 test backend) — a correctness/hardening close with NO new Envoy feature surface; remains the named owner of the pool-liveness carryforwards; (c) TCP-proxy connection pooling (the `upstream_cx_total` TCP carve-out) — a narrower opportunistic close; (d) opening a new §9 family (HTTP/3+QUIC, gRPC, xDS / dynamic config, Observability, Load balancing, Network filters, more HTTP filters, Runtime + hot restart, WASM host) — NOW LEGITIMATE (the family capstone landed at 16; every other §9 Upstream-robustness charter member has a landed minimum-viable phase) but the promised deferred surface closes first; **the phase-18 brainstorm opens a new family deliberately with a clean deferred-surface ledger.** **Chosen rationale:** the budget phase closes promised deferred surface at the lowest architectural risk (no new crate/transport/periodic primitive — two RAII atomics in `envoy-cluster` + two ~10-line gate insertions at existing seams), the highest foundation reuse (the phase-16 retry loop + stateful backend + `Driver::Http1KeepAlive`; the phase-15 conditional-stat-registration discipline + overflow synth-503 + fixture-0023 template), a deterministic timing-robust differential (the §0 zero-cap finding below), and it COMPLETES the Upstream-robustness family in minimum-viable form.

**Critical scoping finding — the zero-cap-always-trips finding (ADR-0046).** A circuit-breaker budget is inherently a CONCURRENCY feature (`max_retries`/`max_requests` cap retries/requests in flight at the same instant), but concurrency-driven differential fixtures are exactly the timing-fragility vector phase 15 explicitly dropped (its SPEC's `Driver::Http1Concurrent`/`--hold-ms` machinery was abandoned at the ADR-0043 re-scope). ### Phase-18 state-1 brainstorm

THIS subsection landed at the **phase-18 state-1 NEW-PHASE brainstorm** (commit `phase 18: state-1 brainstorm — xds-file-based-cds SPEC.md (xDS family opener; dynamic_resources.cds_config.path_config_source initial-load + cluster_manager.cds stats + ClustersConfigDump + fixture 0026) [ADR-0048]`). It records the brainstorm's pick rationale, the alternatives weighed, the three critical scoping findings, and the carryforward inputs the state-2 PLAN-write must consult. Method: cold-start full reads (MISSION / STATE / ROADMAP / DECISIONS [all 48 ADRs] / BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT / SKILL_ROUTING + the phase-17 rollovers ledger) + ONE read-only `Explore` subagent survey of the candidate-family code surfaces at HEAD `49ae04414` (serial dispatch per `feedback_serial_subagent_dispatch`) + direct controller cross-checks. The autonomous pick follows `feedback_pick_recommendation` + MISSION §2.2 (ambiguities → ADR + proceed, never ask mid-phase).

**The family pick (ratified in ADR-0048).** The phase-17 close-out directed this brainstorm to **deliberately open a NEW §9 family with a clean deferred-surface ledger**. The candidates and verdicts:

1. **xDS / dynamic config — CHOSEN**, opened via the filesystem transport (file-based CDS, initial-load-only). The architecturally central remaining family (dynamic config is Envoy's defining capability; D-3.2 names the xDS state machine as core from-scratch work; ADR-0014's protos supersession + the empty BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT "xDS wire state machine" section both wait on it), with a deterministic timing-robust differential at its filesystem entry point and zero new dependencies.
2. **gRPC family — REJECTED (blocked).** gRPC requires HTTP/2 trailer propagation; the code survey confirmed trailers are discarded at HEAD (`crates/envoy-http1/src/client.rs:241-248`; no trailer API in `envoy-http2`). The family opener would have to be trailer plumbing — a prerequisite phase with a thin differential of its own. Revisit once trailers exist.
3. **Load-balancing family — REJECTED (weak deterministic differential).** least_request (P2C random) and random are per-request non-deterministic; ring_hash/maglev are deterministic but demand exact xxHash64 ring/table parity with Envoy (high bilateral-exactness risk, brutal debuggability, no Envoy-side ring introspection); multi-endpoint distinguishable-backend fixture infrastructure does not exist yet.
4. **Observability family — REJECTED (thin-or-heavy).** Tracing/ALS/OTLP need collector infrastructure + span-ID nondeterminism handling; the thin member (access-log format strings, carved out at 06.2) has the least strategic value of any candidate.
5. **HTTP/3+QUIC / WASM host — REJECTED (largest lifts).** Each is a multi-phase foundation sub-project (quinn + UDP listeners + h3spec + an H3 harness driver; resp. a WASM engine + proxy-wasm ABI). Deliberate later picks with their own risk budgets.
6. **Network filters / Runtime + hot restart / more HTTP filters — REJECTED.** Thin members or heavyweight protocol codecs; narrow differential surface; resp. continues an existing family rather than opening a new one.

**The three critical scoping findings (ADR-0048 / SPEC §0):**

1. **The filesystem xDS transport needs NO gRPC, NO protos, NO control plane.** Envoy accepts YAML `path_config_source` files whose `resources` are `@type`-tagged `envoy.config.cluster.v3.Cluster` payloads — exactly the `Cluster` shape the ADR-0014 YAML-native shim already parses for `static_resources.clusters`. One new envelope struct opens the family. The ADR-0014 protos supersession explicitly does NOT fire (deferred to the gRPC-xDS phase).
2. **Initial-load-only is compatible with `ClusterManager`'s post-construction immutability.** The survey confirmed `ClusterManager::from_bootstrap` (`crates/envoy-cluster/src/cluster.rs:721-826`) builds an immutable map with no public mutator. Loading the CDS file at config time, BEFORE construction, requires zero mutability — dynamic clusters enter the same map and every downstream subsystem (pools, TLS, health, outlier, budgets, retries, validators) treats them identically to static clusters (SPEC §5.3). File WATCHING is what needs the mutability refactor → the family's prime deferred follow-up.
3. **The Envoy-side differential surface already exists as allow-listed unasserted names.** Envoy emits `cluster_manager.*` stats + a `ClustersConfigDump` config_dump entry today (fixture 0014 allow-lists the extra entries; fixture 0011's Prometheus set-diff tolerates the extra names). Phase 18 moves them to bilaterally asserted on the CDS fixture — the phase-17 §0-finding-3 pattern repeated.

**Inertness design (the regression-baseline guarantee).** ALL phase-18 surface is conditional on `dynamic_resources.cds_config` being configured: stats register conditionally (the phase-15/17 conditional-registration discipline), the `ClustersConfigDump` entry emits conditionally (fixture 0014 untouched), and no existing fixture configures `dynamic_resources` — so all 25 existing fixtures are byte-identical in expectations and behavior (§7.5 (b)).

**Carryforward inputs for the state-2 PLAN-write (in priority order):** (1) `docs/envoy-rust/phases/18-xds-file-based-cds/SPEC.md` — esp. §6.2 (the 11-item empirical checklist; items 1/4/5 are the ADR-0049 triggers) + §6.1 (the split projection); (2) **ADR-0048** (the scope lock — do NOT re-pick the family or re-litigate the transport choice); (3) the `### Phase-17 rollovers` subsection above (the standing multi-phase Minor inventory — phase 18 engages NONE of it; the pool-liveness family, the H2-upstream-fork gap, the CI readiness-flake family 0011/0012/0022, and the harness-flake cautions all carry unchanged); (4) the fixture 0008 (wire shape) / 0011 + 0014 (allow-list posture) / 0025 (Http1KeepAlive probe + named-stat scrape shape) expectation files; (5) ADR-0014 (the YAML-shim posture phase 18 extends but does NOT supersede) + ADR-0028 (REMAINS OPEN; not engaged).

**Regression baseline phase 18 must keep green (§7.5 (b)):** the **25 Docker-gated differential fixtures `0001`–`0025`** + the h2spec ≥95% conformance gate + the `parse_bootstrap` 28-seed fuzz corpus (→ 29 with the new seed) + the 5 stable-toolchain gates + the 4 standalone-crate builds (`project_isolated_crate_build_blindspot`).

**ADR ledger after this commit:** head **ADR-0048** (count 49). **ADR-0049** reserved for the §6.2 empirical reconciliation (PLAUSIBLE; most-likely trigger: the CDS file envelope shape — the D2 parser is built to it). **ADR-0050** reserved for the §6.1 split (POSSIBLE; projected NOT to fire). **ADR-0014 remains in force; ADR-0028 remains open.**

**The §6.2 verification (PLAN.md "§6.2 empirical lock-ins" L1–L12).** The §0 core findings are CONFIRMED — the xDS family genuinely opens without protos/tonic/control-plane: the bare `resources:` YAML envelope loads (L1); readiness implies loaded, so the fixture is deterministic with zero timing machinery (L2); the `cluster_manager.*` stat tree + `ClustersConfigDump` exist exactly as the differential surface (L3/L5); zero-static-clusters bootstraps are valid (L7); the route-to-dynamic-cluster wire shape is byte-identical to static (L6). **ADR-0049 fired on four reconciliations:** L1 (`@type` required per resource + Envoy's file-extension-driven parser selection → envoy-rust is always-YAML [recorded leniency]; the harness must mount the Envoy-side CDS file at a `.yaml` container path); L4 (Envoy's 3-way negative-path split [missing-path hard-exit / parse-error warn-and-serve + `update_failure` / semantic-error warn-and-serve + `update_rejected`; unknown resource fields warn-accepted] → envoy-rust treats ALL CDS load errors as fatal at startup — the fail-loud posture; recorded divergence; `update_failure`/`update_rejected` register at 0 and are structurally unreachable non-zero); L9 (static/dynamic name collision → static WINS, the CDS entry is skipped as unmodified, no error → envoy-rust mirrors; the SPEC D1 `DuplicateClusterName` reject is DROPPED); L12 (two bootstrap prerequisites: `node.id`+`node.cluster` required with CDS; `validate_clusters: false` required on the route_config → fixture 0026 carries both; `RouteConfiguration.validate_clusters` lands as parse-and-accept; envoy-rust's reference enforcement is defer-then-revalidate-post-merge via `Bootstrap::cds_configured_but_unloaded()` + the `load_dynamic_resources` re-validation). Bonus findings: the stat subset grows 4 → 6 names (`cds.update_attempt`/`cds.update_rejected` are deterministic and cheap); Envoy's `ClustersConfigDump` omits empty keys and carries NO `version_info` when the file has none; the hot-reload item (§6.2 item 11) was INCONCLUSIVE (macOS Docker Desktop virtiofs/inotify limitation — the file-watch follow-up phase must re-verify on Linux CI).

**The SPEC-correction pass (PLAN.md "PLAN-time SPEC corrections").** One anchor drifted: the fuzz corpus is **28 files in the `.gitignore` allow-list but 27 in the test arrays** (`cluster_http2_protocol_options.yaml` allow-listed but absent from the SUCCESS array — a pre-existing inconsistency, likely 13.2-era; carried to the state-5 review inventory; PLAN Task 9 adds the new seed to BOTH and may opportunistically restore the missing entry). Four structural corrections: (1) the config load is SYNC (`std::fs::read_to_string` in envoy-bin `main.rs:49`; `parse_bootstrap` is pure — the SPEC's tokio::fs/async projection is corrected; NO tokio dep lands on envoy-config; the fuzz target stays pure); (2) `AdminHandler::new` already holds `Arc<Bootstrap>` + `Arc<ClusterManager>` (`handler.rs:90-104`) — D5 needs NO signature widening; (3) the cluster-reference checks live at TWO sites (tcp_proxy `bootstrap.rs:2013-2020` + HCM `:2205-2206`) plus the `Http2ClusterFromHttp1Listener` gate's dependent `.expect` (`:2214`) which must be restructured to `if let`; (4) the `all_clusters()` consumer-migration set is 7 sites (validate's per-cluster loop, the 2 reference checks, `envoy_cluster::from_bootstrap`, H1/H2 `PoolManager::for_bootstrap`, `Scheduler::spawn`, the envoy-bin TLS loop) — `OutlierManager` is excluded (it iterates the already-merged ClusterManager).

### Phase-19 state-1 brainstorm

THIS subsection landed at the **phase-19 state-1 NEW-PHASE brainstorm** (commit `phase 19: state-1 brainstorm — xds-file-based-lds SPEC.md (xDS family continuation; dynamic_resources.lds_config.path_config_source initial-load + listener_manager.lds stats + ListenersConfigDump + fixture 0027 canonical LDS+CDS topology) [ADR-0050]`). It records the brainstorm's pick rationale, the alternatives weighed, the four critical scoping findings, and the carryforward inputs the state-2 PLAN-write must consult. Method: cold-start reads (MISSION / STATE / ROADMAP / DECISIONS / BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT / SKILL_ROUTING + the phase-17/18 rollovers ledgers) + ONE read-only `Explore` subagent survey of the candidate code surfaces at HEAD `2044a6bf5` (serial dispatch per `feedback_serial_subagent_dispatch`) + controller cross-checks of every load-bearing claim by direct grep/read. The autonomous pick follows `feedback_pick_recommendation` + MISSION §2.2 (ambiguities → ADR + proceed, never ask mid-phase).

**The continuation pick (ratified in ADR-0050).** The phase-18 close-out directed this brainstorm to weigh the xDS family's prime follow-up against the other §9 families — no phase pre-picked. The candidates and verdicts:

1. **xDS family continuation: file-based LDS — CHOSEN** (`19-xds-file-based-lds`; `dynamic_resources.lds_config.path_config_source`, initial-load-only). The lowest-risk phase the family can offer: every deliverable is a second instantiation of a phase-18 pattern; the differential is deterministic (readiness implies loaded); together with phase 18's CDS it completes Envoy's documented canonical filesystem-dynamic-config topology (fixture 0027).
2. **CDS file watching / hot reload — REJECTED for this phase (three stacked risks + an ROI argument).** (i) The `ClusterManager` mutability refactor is a guaranteed multi-sub-phase split (the survey confirmed immutability + three `Arc<ClusterManager>` holders [envoy-http1 `hcm.rs:114`, envoy-admin `handler.rs:57`, envoy-health `scheduler.rs:42`] + pools/outlier + warming/draining semantics). (ii) A watch fixture is inherently timing-sensitive (write → watch fires → convergence window) — against the timing-robustness doctrine. (iii) **The §6.2 verify-at-PLAN-write discipline cannot run locally**: ADR-0049 Provenance records Envoy's inotify watching is unobservable under macOS Docker Desktop (virtiofs); that phase's §6.2 must be redesigned to run on Linux CI first. (iv) ROI: after LDS (and later RDS/EDS) are file-based, ONE watching phase lights up hot reload for every file-based resource type at once. The watch phase remains the family's prime follow-up — these four points are its entry conditions, recorded for the next brainstorm.
3. **File-based RDS — REJECTED (runner-up; the natural NEXT pick).** Per-HCM config-source topology (`route_config` XOR `rds` schema surgery on a REQUIRED field); per-HCM-scoped stat namespace (`http.<prefix>.rds.<name>.*`); no pre-existing allow-listed Envoy-side surface (fixture 0011 configures no RDS).
4. **File-based EDS — REJECTED.** Needs `ClusterType::Eds` + making `Cluster.load_assignment` conditional (today REQUIRED) — deeper validation-chain surgery than LDS's purely-additive schema. The `LoadAssignment` schema already matches the EDS payload shape (survey-confirmed; recorded for the future EDS phase).
5. **gRPC family — REJECTED (still blocked).** Re-verified at HEAD: trailers still discarded (`crates/envoy-http1/src/client.rs:241-248`); no trailer API in envoy-http2. Unchanged from ADR-0048.
6. **Load-balancing / Observability / HTTP-3+QUIC / WASM host / Network filters / Runtime + hot restart / more HTTP filters — REJECTED.** The ADR-0048 rejection analysis carries unchanged; nothing material changed at HEAD.

**The four critical scoping findings (ADR-0050 / SPEC §0):**

1. **Every phase-18 extension point is a single-variant/single-field reuse.** `ConfigSource`/`PathConfigSource` (`bootstrap.rs:63-79`) reused verbatim for `lds_config`; the `cds.rs` `@type`-tagged envelope (`cds.rs:31-46`) generalizes to `Listener` resources (`type.googleapis.com/envoy.config.listener.v3.Listener`; the existing `Listener` schema at `bootstrap.rs:284-298` parses everything an LDS payload carries); `load_dynamic_resources` (`lib.rs:538`) gains a parallel LDS branch; the harness `{{CDS_PATH}}` machinery (`tests/differential/src/lib.rs:2184-2242`) generalizes to `{{LDS_PATH}}`.
2. **Initial-load-only LDS needs NO listener-manager refactor.** envoy-bin spawns `listeners.first()` (`main.rs:216`); the fixture topology (zero static listeners + one LDS listener) merges at config-load time and `first()` picks the dynamic listener. Zero-static-listeners bootstraps are ALREADY valid in envoy-rust when admin is configured (the validator gate at `bootstrap.rs:1939` rejects only empty-listeners-AND-no-admin). The pre-existing single-traffic-listener limitation is recorded as a deferral, not lifted.
3. **The Envoy-side differential surface pre-exists as allow-listed unasserted names — the third application of this pattern (phases 17 → 18 → 19).** Fixture 0011 allow-lists 12 `listener_manager.*` names as Envoy-only (`expectations.yaml:213-224`); the `listener_manager.lds.*` sub-family appears when `lds_config` is configured (mirroring `cluster_manager.cds.*`). envoy-rust already registers `listener_manager.total_listeners_active` unconditionally (08.2 D14, `envoy-listener/src/lib.rs:184-186`) — it needs only assertion-tightening.
4. **The LDS+CDS composition exercises real new machinery.** Fixture 0027 (an LDS-supplied listener whose HCM routes `/static` → a static cluster and `/dynamic` → a CDS-supplied cluster) is Envoy's documented canonical filesystem topology AND exercises the new §5.7 merge-ordering invariant: dynamic clusters must merge BEFORE dynamic-listener route re-validation — extending phase 18's defer-then-revalidate design (ADR-0049 decision 4) to dynamic-listener routes.

**Inertness design (the regression-baseline guarantee).** ALL phase-19 surface is conditional on `dynamic_resources.lds_config` being configured: the `listener_manager.lds.*` + `listener_added` stats register conditionally (the phase-15/17/18 discipline; `total_listeners_active` is the pre-existing unconditional exception), the `ListenersConfigDump` entry emits conditionally, and no existing fixture configures `lds_config` — so all 26 existing fixtures are byte-identical in expectations and behavior (§7.5 (b)). **Fixture 0026 (which configures `cds_config` but NOT `lds_config`) is the critical inertness witness** — it must see no `listener_manager.lds.*` names and no `ListenersConfigDump` entry; its `configs[1]` ClustersConfigDump index assertion is also the §6.2-item-5 `configs[]`-ordering compatibility trigger.

**Carryforward inputs for the state-2 PLAN-write (in priority order):** (1) `docs/envoy-rust/phases/19-xds-file-based-lds/SPEC.md` — esp. §6.2 (the 11-item empirical checklist; items 1/4/5 are the ADR-0051 triggers) + §6.1 (the split projection) + §5.7 (the merge-ordering invariant); (2) **ADR-0050** (the scope lock — do NOT re-pick the phase or re-litigate the family-continuation choice); (3) **ADR-0049** (the phase-18 §6.2 reconciliation whose decisions extend to LDS where applicable: always-YAML parsing; the all-fatal negative-path posture; the static-wins collision projection; defer-then-revalidate) + **ADR-0048** (the family-opening scope) + **ADR-0014** (the YAML-shim posture, extended a second time) + **ADR-0028** (REMAINS OPEN; not engaged); (4) the `### Phase-18 rollovers` subsection above (the standing multi-phase Minor inventory — phase 19 engages NONE of it; M18-9 [the extract-a-test-support-crate item, the highest-leverage Minor] is again correctly not done inside this phase; the CI readiness-flake family 0011/0012/0022 + the harness-flake cautions carry unchanged); (5) the fixture 0026 files (the structural template for fixture 0027: envoy.yaml/envoy-rust.yaml/cds.yaml/expectations.yaml/README.md) + the phase-18 PLAN.md (the structural template for the phase-19 PLAN) + fixture 0011's `listener_manager.*` allow-list block (`expectations.yaml:213-224` — the names the §2.1 subset draws from).

**Regression baseline phase 19 must keep green (§7.5 (b)):** the **26 Docker-gated differential fixtures `0001`–`0026`** + the h2spec ≥95% conformance gate + the `parse_bootstrap` 29-seed fuzz corpus (→ 30 with the new seed; the corpus is fully consistent entering this phase per the phase-18 carryforward-disposition-1 closure) + the 5 stable-toolchain gates + the 4 standalone-crate builds (`project_isolated_crate_build_blindspot`).

### Phase-19 state-2 PLAN-write

THIS subsection landed at the **phase-19 state-2 standalone PLAN-write** (commit `phase 19: state-2 standalone PLAN-write — PLAN.md + PROGRESS.md skeleton + Task 1 preamble`). **Method.** (1) The HEAVY SPEC §6.2 empirical verification (the ADR-0037→0049 methodology): a single foreground general-purpose subagent ran `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (digest `sha256:56da5afd7df364350ff92de4fb49a9b09957c17295f2899f0a31cd12c28770c2`) under Docker with the LDS+CDS canonical topology (zero static listeners + one static cluster + an LDS file [listener `dynamic_listener`, routes `/static` → `static_backend` + `/dynamic` → `dynamic_backend`] + a CDS file + a host HTTP backend + admin `/stats` + `/config_dump` scrapes), verifying all 11 SPEC §6.2 items; version string `b0f43d67aa25c1b03c97186a200cc187f4c22db3/1.33.0/Clean/RELEASE/BoringSSL`. (2) The PLAN-time SPEC-correction pass: a read-only Explore subagent verified the 16 SPEC §0/§3 anchors at HEAD `8ef6f5b03`; the controller re-verified the load-bearing claims by direct grep (the corpus arithmetic; the `defer_cluster_refs` deferral sites; the envoy-listener Cargo deps; the harness kv-map render flow; the `Http1KeepAliveRequest`/`AdminScrapeCase`/`BodyRule::TextLines` shapes; the `StaticResources.listeners` `#[serde(default)]`). Subagents dispatched SERIALLY per `feedback_serial_subagent_dispatch`.

**The §6.2 outcome — ADR-0051 does NOT fire.** All three trigger items CONFIRM the projections: **L1** (the LDS envelope mirrors the CDS envelope — bare `resources:` + `@type`-tagged Listener payloads; the full DiscoveryResponse shape also accepted; missing `@type` → `lds.update_failure` warn-and-serve in Envoy); **L4** (Envoy's LDS negative-path split exactly mirrors its CDS split: missing file → hard exit / malformed YAML → `lds.update_failure` warn-and-serve / semantic error → `lds.update_rejected` warn-and-serve → envoy-rust's all-fatal posture extends per ADR-0049 decision 2, pre-ratified by ADR-0050; the warn-and-serve divergence classes are recorded at Task 10); **L5** (the `configs[]` order is Bootstrap[0], **Clusters[1], Listeners[2]** — Clusters BEFORE Listeners, so **fixture 0026's `configs[1]` ClustersConfigDump index assertion holds with no amendment**; the ListenersConfigDump nests the listener under `dynamic_listeners[].active_state.listener`). The no-ADR outcome departs from the phase-14→18 cadence (ADR-0041/0043/0045/0047/0049 all fired) because the phase-19 projections were derived from the phase-18 EMPIRICAL findings rather than from documentation, and Envoy's LDS filesystem surface is structurally identical to its CDS surface. **Refinement lock-ins (PLAN-only):** **L6** — LDS-delivered route_configs do NOT require `validate_clusters: false` (Envoy skips inline cluster-reference validation for dynamically-delivered listeners; removing the flag changes nothing). Consequences: fixture 0027's LDS templates carry NO `validate_clusters`; envoy-rust's defer-then-revalidate enforcement (ADR-0050 / SPEC §5.7) is unchanged, and the recorded divergence (an LDS-listener route to a cluster in NEITHER list fails envoy-rust startup vs Envoy's start-and-runtime-503) extends ADR-0049 decision 4's class to LDS routes — recorded in the Task-10 BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT rows, proven by the Task-8 backstop. **L3✧** — `listener_manager.listener_create_success` is PER-WORKER (observed 12 on a 12-core host); excluded from the 6-name subset, never asserted. **L5✧** — `active_state` has no `version_info`; `static_listeners` is absent (not empty) when no static listeners exist. **L7** — static/dynamic listener name collision → static WINS silently (the CDS L9 mirror; envoy-rust mirrors with collision-skip + warn). **L11** — duplicate-address in one LDS update → `lds.update_rejected` (NOT `listener_create_failure`), non-atomic application; irrelevant to envoy-rust (the TooManyListeners gate covers it); the backstop uses missing-file/malformed-file/name-collision/unresolved-route negative paths instead.

**The five PLAN-time corrections:** (1) the D3 consumer-migration sweep is **5 sites**, not 4 — the SPEC missed the `NoRuntime` gate (`bootstrap.rs:1939`), distinct from the `TooManyListeners` gate (`:1934`); (2) the `NoRuntime` gate needs the `lds_configured_but_unloaded()` deferral (the phase-18 `defer_cluster_refs` pattern applied to a second gate; the `TooManyListeners` gate just migrates to `all_listeners().count()` and re-checks naturally post-merge); (3) the D4 registration site is a new `envoy_listener::register_lds_stats(bootstrap, registry)` free function — unit-testable in-crate (envoy-listener already depends on envoy-config + envoy-stats, so no new dependency edge; `Listener::bind` is the wrong site: it runs per-listener with no bootstrap access, while the lds.* family is a once-per-process load fact); (4) the corpus arithmetic: 29 = 25 SUCCESS + 3 REJECT + 1 minimal → Task 9 makes it 30 = 26 + 3 + 1; (5) **the LDS templates are PER-SIDE** (`lds-envoy.yaml` + `lds-envoy-rust.yaml`) — the SPEC's shared-`lds.yaml` projection cannot work because the LDS payload carries the HCM, whose Envoy-only fields (`generate_request_id` + `route_config.request_headers_to_remove`, needed for byte-exact echo bodies) are rejected by envoy-rust's `deny_unknown_fields` parser; the per-side convention mirrors the existing `envoy.yaml`/`envoy-rust.yaml` main-config convention; `cds.yaml` stays a shared template.
